clue.text: Soldier's plot to be a freeloader

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper; the 's is just a possessive link
a plot of land is a site

explanation.surface: A soldier's scheme to live off others without paying his way.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is someone who lives off others, sponging, just as a freeloader does.

clue.text: Pawn books when hospital supplies chemical compound

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone pawns their books while a hospital provides a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' looks like a verb for hocking goods, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is potassium carbonate or a related potassium salt, a chemical compound used in fertiliser.

clue.text: Warden initially registered indignation

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: indignation is anger at unfair treatment

explanation.surface: A warden first recorded his outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a keeper or warden of a park or forest.

clue.text: Despatch spring flower

parts.note: despatch as a noun means haste or speed
a spring of water is a well

explanation.surface: Send off a springtime bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despatch' looks like a verb meaning send, and 'spring' like the season; both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Veronica.

clue.text: Confident Barbarian enters the fun of the game

indicators.note: the pieces enter the fun word, going inside it

parts.note: a treat is a source of fun or pleasure
sure means confident
the Huns were a barbarian people

explanation.surface: A self-assured Barbarians rugby player joins in the fun of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B hints at the Barbarians, a famous invitational rugby team; here it is just a Hun.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure hunt is a game in which players follow clues to find a hidden prize.

clue.text: Tory leader taking part in hunt is virtuous

indicators.note: the Tory letter is taking part in the hunt, so it goes inside that word

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of Tory is used

explanation.surface: A Conservative grandee who rides with the hunt is nonetheless morally upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and morally good, especially sexually, a close synonym of virtuous.

clue.text: Drawback for couple

definitions.meaning: to couple is to fasten or attach, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A downside to being in a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or drawback; to hitch is to hook one thing to another, coupling them.

clue.text: Rob's more awkward in a hat

indicators.note: awkward letters are ungainly and out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rob looks more clumsy wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Fundamental principles of weather

definitions.meaning: the basics or rudiments of a subject
the forces of nature, wind and rain, as in being exposed to bad conditions

explanation.surface: The basic rules of meteorology.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements are a subject's rudiments, and also the wind and rain of bad weather.

clue.text: Offered and was inclined to embrace soldier

indicators.note: one word holding another in its arms means the first wraps around the second

parts.note: tended means was inclined or disposed
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone offered something and felt like hugging a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to formally offer, as in tendering a resignation or a bid.

clue.text: Block major road going through eyesore?

indicators.note: a road going through something passes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a stye is literally a sore on the eyelid
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI here

explanation.surface: A planning complaint: block the motorway that cuts through an ugly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' reads as an ugly building but is taken literally: a sore on the eye. The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; the 1 serves as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, which is what blocking someone's plans does.

clue.text: Speaker keeps royal box for the organiser

indicators.note: one word keeps the others, holding them within

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in Rex or Regina
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: The Speaker holds a royal box for the event's organiser.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestrator arranges and coordinates events, an organiser behind the scenes.

clue.text: Use up change aboard ship

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vessel is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them
P for penny, a coin of small change

explanation.surface: A sailor uses up their loose change while on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aboard ship' tempts a solver to put something inside SS; here 'ship' is the verb meaning send.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money or energy is to use it up.

clue.text: Heave when swallowing fish supplement

indicators.note: one word swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a heave of the sea is a surge
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Retching while eating fish, of all things a food supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra charge added on, a supplement to the basic price.

clue.text: Be pessimistic about weather — frost is widespread

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloom about the forecast: frost is everywhere, so expect the worst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals the rearrangement; 'is widespread' could equally be the signal and adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear the worst is the idiom for expecting the bad outcome, which is pessimism.

clue.text: Miscreant forced Roger down

indicators.note: letters forced out of shape are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain pushed Roger to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or breaks the law, an offender.

clue.text: Store ice produced in secret

indicators.note: letters produced afresh are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Keeping ice made in a clandestine way.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a select few, obscure or secret.

clue.text: Smirk when taking in this month in Ireland

indicators.note: one word taking in another holds it inside

parts.note: a leer is a sly, knowing look, close to a smirk
inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone smirks on being told of an event in Ireland this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inst' is an old commercial abbreviation: 'your letter of the 5th inst' meant the 5th of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of the Irish nation, a region found there.

clue.text: Athletes wrongly appear to be the outstanding performers

indicators.note: letters put together wrongly are out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to show up is to appear

explanation.surface: Athletes mistakenly seem to think they are the stars of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to outshine everyone else, being the most impressive performers present.

clue.text: Walk round Oxfordshire town is transfixing

definitions.meaning: Goring-on-Thames, a large village by the river
piercing through, as a bull does with its horns

parts.note: to go somewhere is to walk there
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A walk around a country town is captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a place on the Thames in Oxfordshire, an English county west of London; a second meaning is impaling with horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Goring is a Thames-side village; goring also means piercing with horns, which is transfixing.

clue.text: Spanish leaders present in province

parts.note: the leading pair of letters in Spanish, also its standard abbreviation Sp
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: Leaders from Spain are attending in a region.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a domain of activity or influence, a province in the figurative sense.

clue.text: No writer got into a row for a utensil

indicators.note: the pieces got into the row, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
taken as written
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: No writer got into a quarrel over a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line of seats: a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is a kitchen utensil for opening cans.

clue.text: Penny's covering evidence

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny; the 's is just a link
a roof is a covering for a building

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny is concealing the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is the coin, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes a fact.

clue.text: Band of Greek publishers

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A band of musicians belonging to Greek publishers.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of musicians is a group, as in a pop group.

clue.text: Limit relationship with knight

parts.note: a ratio is a numerical relationship between two quantities
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Limit your relationship with a knight, perhaps a courtly romance advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration something is to restrict or limit how much is allowed.

clue.text: Taro cooked — hunger for drug

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to pine is to yearn or hunger for something

explanation.surface: Cooked taro root, a craving for a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a drug obtained from deadly nightshade, used to dilate the pupils.

clue.text: Vessel for a service in church

indicators.note: these pieces go in the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A container used during a service in church, such as a wine flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service; it is the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass flask for serving water or wine, so a vessel.

clue.text: Master villain to suspend a meeting

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is a master of a craft
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A criminal mastermind plotting to halt a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue is to discontinue a parliamentary session without dissolving it, suspending the assembly.
